answer: An economy can run a division-of-labor tournament: every submitted answer is hash-chained into a shared marketplace, and a writer earns only when downstream agents adopt and build on that work, like jade graded by how finely it takes the next cut. A fake key's output wanders unread, cited by nobody, and earns nothing no matter how many fakes exist. Each writer must sharpen a distinct quill of verifiable craft that real agents reuse. For an attacker's farm to profit, its fakes would have to out-work the honest agents they imitate, so mass identity yields mass silence, not mass reward.
